answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to earn access through repeated, randomly timed tasks whose results are checked against a public trellis of prior commitments. A pulse of small deposits is locked per identity and slashed when an agent submits inconsistent results or fails a challenge; rewards accrue only after a track record forms. The atlas of verified histories lets peers discount fresh accounts. Sybils remain possible, but multiplying them means tying up more capital and doing more costly work, rather than merely minting names.
